hurricane.en: Hurricanes are found in the Atlantic, Cyclones in the Indian Ocean and Typhoons in the West Pacific.
hurricane.zh: 在大西洋被称为飓风，在印度洋被称为气旋，在西太平洋被称为台风。

hurricane.en: What else causes loss of life in a hurricane, typhoon or cyclone?
hurricane.zh: 在飓风、台风或气旋中，还有什么会导致人员伤亡？

hurricane.en: Maybe becoming seriously ill, or experiencing a natural disaster like a hurricane or an earthquake, or living through a conflict.
hurricane.zh: 也许是得了重病，或者经历了飓风或地震等自然灾害，抑或是经历了冲突。

hurricane.en: But it’s not just in living things. Hurricane spirals, galaxies, and even the structure of DNA reflect this ratio, almost as if the universe itself is built on a foundation of mathematical elegance.
hurricane.zh: 但这不仅存在于生物中。飓风螺旋、星系，甚至 DNA 的结构都反映了这个比例，几乎就像宇宙本身就是建立在数学优雅的基础之上一样。

hum.en: Fusty, reeking, toiking, honking, humming, funky… Smells are everywhere, whether they're bad smells like rotten eggs and sweaty feet, or pleasant ones like lavender and freshly baked bread.
hum.zh: 发霉味(fusty)、恶臭(reeking)、toiking、honking、humming、funky……气味无处不在，无论是臭鸡蛋、汗脚这样难闻的气味，还是薰衣草、新鲜出炉面包这样宜人的气味。

hum.en: Listening to Michael Rosen's list – funky, reeking, humming and the rest – you might think English is good at describing smells, but in fact, all those words really mean is bad smelling.
hum.zh: 听了 Michael Rosen 列出的那些词——funky、reeking、humming 等等——你可能会觉得英语很擅长描述气味，但事实上，这些词的意思其实都只是'难闻'而已。

hum.en: He watched the forests around him being cut down by developers; he saw aircraft flying overhead, he heard the distant hum of industrial progress, and grew convinced that technology was spreading like a disease.
hum.zh: 他看着身边的森林被开发商砍伐；他看到飞机从头顶飞过，听到远处工业进步的嗡嗡声，并坚信技术正像疾病一样蔓延。

humanity.en: What happened next was called by Human Rights Watch a crime against humanity.
humanity.zh: 接下来发生的事情被“人权观察”组织称为反人类罪。

humanity.en: This would require an unimaginable amount of energy—far beyond what humanity could ever generate.
humanity.zh: 这将需要难以想象的巨大能量——远远超过人类所能产生的能量。

humanity.en: The power of deep reading is really fundamental to our humanity.
humanity.zh: 深度阅读的力量对我们的人性至关重要。

humanity.en: So the idea that working hard doesn't make progress is one of the biggest farces that exists in humanity.
humanity.zh: 所以，“努力工作不能取得进展”这种想法是人类社会中最大的谎言之一。

humanity.en: An unfortunate truth about humanity is that we humans are capable of committing acts against our fellow humans that are utterly inhumane.
humanity.zh: 关于人性，有一个令人遗憾的事实：人类有能力对同类做出极其残忍、毫无人性的事情。

hurt.en: A person who is tolerant of something is able to endure it without being hurt.
hurt.zh: 一个对某事 tolerant（耐受）的人能够忍受它而不受伤害。

hurt.en: Being tolerant of something means being able to endure it without getting hurt.
hurt.zh: 对某事 tolerant（耐受）意味着能够忍受它而不受伤害。

hurt.en: She said she’d been tricked–by the devil, she claimed–and hadn’t meant to hurt anyone.
hurt.zh: 她说自己当时受了蛊惑——她声称是魔鬼干的——并不是故意要伤害任何人。

hurt.en: I didn't cry because she was hurt. I didn't, I was like, it's over.
hurt.zh: 我不是因为她受伤而哭。我不是，我当时想，结束了。

hurt.en: Someone who is emotionally vulnerable has their feelings and emotions easily hurt.
hurt.zh: 情感脆弱（emotionally vulnerable）的人是指其感情和情绪容易受到伤害的人。

humour.en: We often use exaggeration for emphasis or for humour – something known as hyperbole.
humour.zh: 我们经常为了强调或幽默而使用夸张法——也就是所谓的 hyperbole。

humour.en: The team at Dictionary.com described it as “a playful, Gen Alpha expression of absurdist internet humour”.
humour.zh: Dictionary.com 的团队将它描述为“一种俏皮的、阿尔法世代式的、带有荒诞色彩的网络幽默表达”。

humour.en: We know that Caligula loved playing jokes and had a devilish sense of humour, and it seems much more probable that either he was planning on doing this to ridicule his senators, or that he made a passing comment along the lines of “so and so is so useless that my horse could govern better than they could”.
humour.zh: 我们知道 Caligula 喜欢开玩笑，并且有着恶魔般的幽默感，似乎更有可能是他当时正计划这样做来羞辱他的元老院议员，或者他只是顺口说了一句类似“某某某太废物了，我的马都比他治理得好”这样的话。

humorous.en: Mr. Trevor Noah, the former host of The Daily Show, where he gained a massive following for his humorous yet incisive take on politics and society.
humorous.zh: Trevor Noah先生，The Daily Show的前任主持人，他因对政治和社会幽默而深刻的见解而收获了大量粉丝。

humorous.en: Yeah, or as my daughters would say, "I've had a mare today." And when they say mare, which is obviously shortened from 'nightmare', what it basically means is they've had a mild and potentially slightly humorous occurrence at work.
humorous.zh: 是的，或者像我女儿们会说的，“我今天过得很 mare。”当她们说 mare 时，这显然是 nightmare 的缩写，其基本意思是她们在工作中遇到了一些轻微的、可能还有点幽默的小插曲。

hunt.en: Australia’s first people would have hunted kangaroos and emus and also much smaller animals.
hunt.zh: 澳大利亚的第一代原住民会猎捕袋鼠、鸸鹋以及体型小得多的动物。

hunt.en: Dogs bred for hunting, with speed, stamina, and an exceptional sense of smell.
hunt.zh: 为狩猎而培育的狗，具备速度、耐力和非凡的嗅觉。

hunt.en: It was designed for crowds to gather there and watch gladiator fights or animal hunts.
hunt.zh: 它旨在让民众聚集在那里观看角斗士决斗或猎兽表演。

hunt.en: The fires would encourage new plant growth and also attract animals to hunt.
hunt.zh: 大火会促进新植物的生长，同时也会吸引动物供他们猎取。

hunt.en: Often, though not always, cooking became associated more with women, and hunting more with men.
hunt.zh: 虽然并非总是如此，但通常烹饪更多地与女性联系在一起，而狩猎则更多地与男性联系在一起。

hunger.en: These were driven by hunger and exhaustion and anger at the people who had put Germany into a war.
hunger.zh: 这些是由饥饿、精疲力竭以及对把德国拖入战争的人的愤怒所驱使的。

hunger.en: And as for the quantities, they were calculated to be just enough to stop you dying of hunger, but nothing more.
hunger.zh: 至于分量，计算得刚刚好让你不至于饿死，仅此而已。

hunger.en: This was not luxurious food. Hunger and starvation were actually serious risks for people across Britain, across Europe at the time.
hunger.zh: 这并不是奢侈的食物。在当时的英国和整个欧洲，饥饿和挨饿实际上是人们面临的严重风险。

hunger.en: Hunger and food had captured their minds.
hunger.zh: 饥饿和食物已经占据了他们的心智。

hunger.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam. Today, we have a story that will change the way you think about many things - poverty, loneliness, time, even hunger.
hunger.zh: 我是 Shankar Vedantam。今天，我们有一个故事，它将改变你对许多事物的看法——贫穷、孤独、时间，甚至是饥饿。

humiliation.en: What replaced him was a ruler who seemed to revel in cruelty, humiliation, and excess.
humiliation.zh: 取代他的是一个似乎以残忍、羞辱和无节制为乐的统治者。

humiliation.en: They stripped some prisoners naked as a form of humiliation.
humiliation.zh: 他们把一些囚犯的衣服扒光，作为一种羞辱手段。

humiliation.en: Their mother to the women's. Chaplin said later that the humiliations of those years were what made him who he was.
humiliation.zh: 他们的母亲去了女性病房。卓别林后来表示，那几年所遭受的屈辱塑造了他的人生。

humiliation.en: The participants were subjected to extreme stress, humiliation, and emotional trauma —all things that researchers today are required to avoid.
humiliation.zh: 参与者承受了极端的压力、羞辱和情感创伤——这些都是今天的研究者被要求必须避免的。

humiliation.en: And when it wasn’t humiliation and sexual depravity, he is also remembered by historians as an ineffective and cowardly leader of Rome.
humiliation.zh: 当他不搞羞辱和性堕落时，历史学家也记住了他作为一个无能且懦弱的罗马领袖。

humanitarian.en: Otto Warmbier would be released on humanitarian grounds.
humanitarian.zh: 奥托·瓦姆比尔将以人道主义理由获释。

humanitarian.en: He fought in Iraq, Afghanistan, and elsewhere, and has now has written a book called The Heart and the Fist: The Education of a Humanitarian, the Making of a Navy SEAL.
humanitarian.zh: 他在伊拉克、阿富汗和其他地方战斗过，现在写了一本名为《心与拳：一个人道主义者的教育，一个海豹突击队员的炼成》（The Heart and the Fist: The Education of a Humanitarian, the Making of a Navy SEAL）的书。

humanitarian.en: Today, Curie is remembered for her extraordinary discoveries, for coining the term radioactivity and also for her humanitarian work in creating x-ray machines and helping during World War I.
humanitarian.zh: 今天，人们铭记居里夫人是因为她非凡的发现、她创造了“放射性”一词，以及她在第一次世界大战期间制造 X 光机和参与救援的人道主义工作。

humanitarian.en: Yet the darker sides of his rule remain impossible to ignore: the silencing of critics, the imprisonment of activists, the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Yemen, and the unresolved questions around the murder of Jamal Khashoggi.
humanitarian.zh: 然而，他统治中较黑暗的一面依然无法忽视：对批评人士的禁声、对活动人士的监禁、也门持续的人道主义危机，以及围绕 Jamal Khashoggi 谋杀案尚未解决的疑问。

huddle.en: To the 500 or so Puritans huddled in their icy wooden homes, he was an ever-present enemy, lurking in the shadows, waiting to snatch their souls.
huddle.zh: 对于挤在冰冷木屋里的那大约500名清教徒来说，他是无处不在的敌人，潜伏在阴影中，随时准备夺走他们的灵魂。

hush.en: Local lore described it in hushed tones —this was no simple village of huts, but something far older, far grander.
hush.zh: 当地的传说低声描述着它——这不是一个简单的茅草村落，而是某种更加古老、更加宏伟的东西。

hut.en: Local lore described it in hushed tones —this was no simple village of huts, but something far older, far grander.
hut.zh: 当地的传说低声描述着它——这不是一个简单的茅草村落，而是某种更加古老、更加宏伟的东西。

hull.en: The idea was to creep up, undetected, on British ships and plant a bomb on the ship’s hull, the side of the ship, and then rush away before the bomb exploded.
hull.zh: 这个想法是悄悄地、不被察觉地靠近英国船只，在船体即船的侧面安放一枚炸弹，然后在炸弹爆炸前迅速逃离。

hug.en: This hug that you're getting from your friend is the most important thing you will ever experience.
hug.zh: 你从朋友那里得到的这个拥抱是你将要经历的最重要的事情。

hug.en: She even like pushes me off sometimes. Like I hug her hard, hug her hard and I hug her for long.
hug.zh: 她甚至有时会把我推开。就像我用力拥抱她，用力拥抱她，我拥抱了很久。

humble.en: And so that's why probably, at least for me, when people are like, whatever the trait is, like, he's so humble, he's so whatever, like, you probably will never feel like you have the trait.
humble.zh: 但你仍然可以基于证据而不是情绪来拥有这个特质。
